title: QuaRot Mirror coordinate sweep
hypothesis: A one-angle hidden-channel gauge selected on development data lowers int4 quantization distortion over identity and a fixed Hadamard gauge while preserving full-precision function; compare to direct learned Givens-angle control and charge actual payload bytes.
physical_object: Two shared 8x8 linear layers with an 8D hidden gauge
mirror_coordinate: One Givens angle rotates hidden basis: W1'=W1R, W2'=R^T W2; rotations are folded into quantized weights
logical_multiplicity: Equivalent full-precision gauges for one function; not independent functions

development.selection_metric: aggregate normalized output MSE after per-matrix symmetric int4 quantization

fresh.angle: single development-selected angle frozen for all fresh worlds

controls: direct learned scalar Givens angle using identical frozen value (SpinQuant-style attribution control)

storage.authority: actual serialized NPZ inference payload bytes
storage.quantization: symmetric per-matrix signed int4, nibble packed; scales and method metadata charged
paid_objects: full precision matrices for upper reference

success_gate: Fresh angle gauge preserves full-precision function before quantization, reduces mean NRMSE >=20% versus both identity and Hadamard on every world, and Mirror payload <=50% of full precision.
failure_gate: Gauge equivalence fails, no fresh quantization-quality improvement over QuaRot controls, or direct scalar-angle control exactly aliases the Mirror candidate (Mirror-specificity failure).
boundaries: Synthetic 2-layer linear quantization screen only; no LLM/NLL, GPU, energy or natural quantized model evidence.
The task studies representation conditioning under quantization, not functional capacity.
Learned rotations are prior art (SpinQuant); any gain is attributed only to this screened gauge choice, not a new rotation principle.
